title: Adoption Sentinel: KV Eviction Scenarios & Scheduler Conformance (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines an 'Adoption Sentinel' pattern for admitting new model variants (including quantized/optimized kernels) into the speculative-serving path and describes the KV-cache eviction semantics, scheduler conformance checks, and rollout/rollback triggers we will use during canary and ramp phases. The goal is to reduce user-visible regressions while enabling aggressive performance optimizations.

Scope and motivation:
- Applies to any model variant that will be eligible for speculative early-emission or different kernel families (e.g., F32 -> Q4_K_MIX, attention-kernel-A -> kernel-B).
- We focus on two operational failure modes: correctness regressions (log-prob distribution changes, tokenization mismatches) and cache/scheduler instability (KV corruption, increased latency tail due to eviction thrashing).
- Current onboarding lacks a lightweight runtime sentinel that enforces invariants during traffic-weighted rollout. This causes delayed rollbacks or noisy rollouts.

High-level design:
1) Adoption Sentinel: lightweight per-node agent co-located with runtime. Responsibilities:
   - Observe per-request kernel selection and KV cache footprints.
   - Maintain short-lived trial-traces for candidate variants (max 1s or N tokens).
   - Emit a conformance verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) to the control plane with attached metrics.
   - Support manual override and automated abort based on policy.

2) KV eviction semantics (eviction-ripple model):
   - Use a two-tier watermark: soft_watermark (per-shard target), hard_watermark (absolute cap).
   - On crossing soft_watermark: signal scheduler to throttle admitting new speculative trials for the variant; continue serving existing inflight requests.
   - On crossing hard_watermark: trigger immediate admission freeze + background targeted evictions using LRU-Buckets per context to avoid cross-context staleness.
   - Eviction ripple: eviction should preferentially remove entries from contexts with low recency and no pinned sessions. If eviction causes spike > 2x tail latency, revert to conservative eviction policy (per-request linear scan rather than bulk).

3) Scheduler conformance checks (what sentinel validates):
   - Kernel Routing Determinism: for identical input prefix and runtime flags, kernel selection must be deterministic. Non-determinism -> WARN.
   - KV Consistency After Handoff: after a kernel handoff, the receiving kernel must observe identical KV-cache prefix entries for the same request id and sequence. Any mismatch -> FAIL.
   - Emission Latency Bound: speculative early emission must not increase p99 by more than 15% relative to baseline for the same qps/bsz profile.
   - Memory Accounting: candidate kernels must report accurate delta allocation metrics within 5% of observed consumption.

Acceptance criteria for model variant when assessed by sentinel:
- Functional parity checks: token-level equivalence on seeded test prompts (approximate equality using top-k/backoff heuristics allowed for quantized variants).
- Metric thresholds (all must be true to PASS):
  * inference-p95 <= baseline-p95 * 1.1
  * inference-p99 <= baseline-p99 * 1.15
  * cache-miss-rate <= baseline-miss-rate + 0.02 absolute
  * cross-context-kv-corruption-rate == 0 over 10k trial requests
- No FAIL-level KV inconsistencies observed in 30m rolling window.

Rollout and automated rollback policy:
- Canary: send 1% traffic for 30m. Sentinel must report PASS for last 10m before ramp. If WARN observed, hold and notify owners. If FAIL -> immediate rollback and mark variant quarantined.
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 15–30m stabilization windows. Sentinel must emit PASS for each window's last 10m.
- Auto-rollback triggers: any of the following cause instant rollback:
  * cross-context-kv-corruption detected
  * sudden p99 spike > 2x baseline lasting > 2m
  * hard_watermark hit on >80% of nodes for >1m while candidate is admitted
  * token-level divergence ratio > configured threshold (see below)

Automatic mitigation (post-rollback):
- On rollback, runtime must:
  1) freeze admissions for the variant,
  2) drain inflight speculative trials to completion without starting new ones,
  3) trigger a targeted KV scan to detect and repair inconsistent entries (if repair path exists),
  4) publish full dump to diagnostics bucket and alert SRE/owners.

Metrics to capture (sentinel emits these with each verdict):
- per-variant: trial-requests, trial-successes, trial-fails, p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-latency-spike-count, kernel-switch-count, avg-kv-entries-per-request, cache-miss-rate, eviction-rate, time-to-recovery-after-eviction (ms).
- safety: cross-context-kv-corruption-count, kv-read-verification-failures, prefix-equivalence-failures, RCU-reconcile-count.
- economic/ops: effective-tokens-per-second, cpu-gpu-hours-per-10k-requests, amortized-cost-delta.

Operational runbook (short):
- Pre-roll checklist:
  * validate unit tests for model and kernels in CI (see PR #897).
  * run local sentinel simulation on staging for at least 10k requests.
  * ensure KMS keys and audit logging are enabled for private modes.
- Canary phase:
  * watch sentinel PASS/WARN/FAIL stream.
  * if WARN: sample 200 request traces and compare token-level diffs.
  * if FAIL: follow automated rollback and open triage ticket with linked traces.
- Post-rollback analysis:
  * correlate kernel-switch-count spikes with eviction events.
  * check for scheduling hot-spots (single node receiving disproportionate speculative trials).

Unresolved questions / design trade-offs:
1) Repair vs. quarantine: do we attempt in-place KV repair for minor inconsistency (reconcile using authoritative master) or always quarantine variant until manual fix? Trade-off: repair reduces churn but risks silent corruption. Tentative stance: default to quarantine; allow opt-in auto-repair behind an admin flag.
2) Consistency watermark tuning: what is sane default soft/hard watermarks per GPU class? Need offline capacity grid and e2e experiments to propose numbers.
3) Determinism enforcement: some kernel families rely on non-deterministic optimizations for speed. How strict should deterministic routing be? Proposed: record non-determinism as WARN and require owners to justify and add compensating checks.

Implementation notes / API sketches:
- Sentinel accepts a light RPC: POST /sentinel/verdict with payload {variant_id, node_id, verdict, metrics_blob, samples_url}. Sampling must include raw model logits for first N tokens for offline diffs.
- Runtime exposes a read-only per-request diagnostic stream when trial active (max 5kB per request) to avoid sensitive leaks; samples are only stored in secured diagnostics buckets.

Local experiments to run (owners):
- Stress test variant with artificially constrained KV capacity to provoke eviction ripple and observe p99 divergence.
- Compare two scheduling strategies: immediate-throttle vs admission-window. Measure rollback frequency under both.

TODOs and action items:
- [ ] Marcus: prototype sentinel agent binary that collects kernel-switch events (ONB-482).
- [ ] Evelyn: run eviction-ripple simulation on staging cluster and propose soft/hard watermarks.
- [ ] Diego: add token-level diff sampler to the runtime and hook into diagnostics bucket.
- [ ] Asha: draft proposal for admin-auto-repair flag and failure modes.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc prioritizes safe defaults: quarantine on FAIL, conservative evictions, and explicit manual opt-in for aggressive repairs.
- Looking for feedback on: acceptable WARN thresholds, watermark defaults per GPU SKU, and whether to allow non-deterministic kernels in the speculative path if compensating checks are present.

References:
- See ONB-482, PR #897 (runtime kernel routing hooks), Slack thread RFC: C01A9B2C3.

Appendix: quick example sequences (for engineers)
1) Happy path (PASS):
   - Node receives trial request for variant V1 (1% traffic).
   - Kernel A selected deterministically, KV footprint 12 entries.
   - Sentinel records p95 within budget, reports PASS.
   - Control plane increments traffic to next stage.
2) Eviction ripple -> WARN:
   - KV usage hits soft_watermark on node X.
   - Sentinel marks WARN and reduces admission of new trials on node X for V1 for 2m.
   - Overall ramp is paused; owners alerted.
3) FAIL and rollback:
   - Cross-context KV mismatch discovered for request id R123.
   - Sentinel emits FAIL, control plane triggers rollback.
   - Runtime freezes new admissions, drains inflight trials, starts targeted scan and publishes traces.

---
End of draft.
